nowweather.config.entry.shaders_cloudrai: 0.60 by default, and the contract value of NW_CLOUD_BAND in the shader pack. Change it and you must change NW_CLOUD_BAND in Lib/IndividualFounctions/NowWeather.glsl too, or the cloud cover stops lining up (lower it and overcast never reaches full cloud; raise it and the cloud curve gets squashed)
nowweather.config.entry.shaders_cloudtor: Uses real cloud cover to darken the sky, with or without shaders (cloud cover uses rainLevel 0.00–0.60)
nowweather.config.entry.shaders_intensit: Writes continuous rain and thunder intensity into rainLevel so shaders can tell drizzle from a downpour (precipitation uses 0.75–1.00)
nowweather.config.entry.shaders_rainamou: Fine-tune how heavy the rain looks. Multiplied into the precipitation intensity before it is encoded into the shader's rain band: 0.5 makes moderate rain look light, 1.0 is unchanged, 2.0 makes light rain look moderate, and 0.0 draws no rain overlay at all (the weather is still "raining"). Only the value inside the precipitation band is changed, so the encoded value never drops below 0.75 — you cannot end up with "says it is raining but nothing renders".
nowweather.config.entry.shaders_snowamou: Fine-tune how heavy the snow looks. Same mechanism as the rain amount scale, but applied only to frozen precipitation (light/moderate/heavy snow, blizzard, sleet, freezing rain, hail). Use this rather than the rain scale to make snow thinner or thicker.
